title: Ancient introgression drives wild boar expansion and phenotypic diversification of domestic pigs.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file could be opened because none could be located. Checked: Europe PMC (paper flagged not open access, no PMC identifier, no supplementary file list, no text-mined accessions); PubMed XML record for PMID 42784680 (no DataBank/accession list); NCBI elink from PubMed to GEO/SRA/BioProject (no links); NCBI BioProject searches by title ('wild boar', 'Sus scrofa' + Eurasia) and by submitter ('Huazhong Agricultural University', 'Yazhouwan') - the only 2026 wild-boar resequencing projects found (PRJNA1416623, 30 sequencing runs; PRJNA1416629) are from a different institution and far too small for 745 genomes; Chinese National Genomics Data Center GSA search for 'wild boar' (no matching CRA/PRJCA accession); Zenodo/Dryad DOI search (nothing); Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall (one green copy only, at Cardiff University's repository, which returns HTTP 403 to every request, so the data availability statement itself is unreadable); publisher page returns HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study content: 745 pig and wild boar genomes from 58 populations, 256 of them newly sequenced from South and Southeast Asia, 3 new reference genome assemblies, a ~43 megabase introgressed X-chromosome haplotype, and the claim that it carries loci for body size and cold adaptation. These come from the abstract plus the institutional press release (Huazhong Agricultural University), not from any file.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No downloadable dataset could be found by any route: no accession in PubMed, no NCBI BioProject/SRA link, no Chinese GSA deposit found, no Zenodo/Dryad record, and the data availability statement is unreadable because the article is paywalled (Science, not in PubMed Central) and the single green open-access copy is blocked (HTTP 403). Even if an accession exists, what would be deposited is raw whole-genome sequencing reads for 745 pigs, which the project rules forbid downloading.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no measured phenotype column per animal. Body size and cold tolerance are discussed as traits of breeds and populations, and the body-size loci come from previously published association studies, so any label would have to be constructed by attaching breed-level or literature-derived trait values to individual genomes.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified. Inputs would be genotypes derived from raw sequencing reads; no variant call file (VCF) or genotype matrix was found anywhere.

a5_enough_rows.note: The modelling unit would be the animal: 745 individuals, below the ~1,500-row bar for regression and only moderately above the 400-row classification bar, and I could not confirm any per-animal table exists.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; raw reads for 745 genomes would be tens of terabytes
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL on size. Whole-genome resequencing of 745 pigs at typical coverage is far beyond a 16 GB laptop and beyond the project's 50 MB download / ~5 GB working-set limits, and no small processed derivative was found.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot check: nothing to count. The abstract says 745 genomes and the press release adds 58 populations and 256 newly sequenced samples; no file exists to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: The introgression calls, local ancestry tracts and selection signals that would be the most natural targets are themselves outputs of the authors' inference pipeline, so training on them would be distilling their method rather than learning from a measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim can be stated, because no dataset could be located or opened; any model would rest on genotypes we cannot obtain and on phenotype labels the study does not record per animal.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use pig genome variation to predict body size and cold tolerance of wild and domestic pig populations
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: genotypes across the genome for each of the 745 wild boar and domestic pig individuals, especially the ~43 megabase stretch of the X chromosome the paper highlights. Number of usable examples verified: none, because no genotype file was found.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: an animal's body size class (or adult weight) and whether its population lives in a cold climate. The true answer would have to come from breed records and climate data attached afterwards, not from a measurement column in the study.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Pig breeders and evolutionary geneticists would like to know which inherited DNA segments drive the tenfold weight range across pig populations; here the idea fails before it starts because neither the genotypes nor per-animal traits are obtainable.

ml_idea: Considered: predict population-level body size and cold adaptation from genome-wide genotypes, or predict archaic-introgression status of a genomic window from sequence features. Both die at the data stage - no obtainable genotype table and no per-animal measured trait.

effort.compute_note: No estimate possible: no file sizes were obtainable. By reference, raw reads for 745 pig genomes would be tens of terabytes, which rules out the laptop regardless.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a deposited accession and a processed variant file - done, and it killed the project in under an hour: no accession is discoverable and the data availability statement sits behind a paywall plus a blocked repository copy.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails as verified: no dataset is reachable. The Science article is paywalled and absent from PubMed Central, the one green open-access copy returns HTTP 403, PubMed lists no databank accessions, NCBI BioProject/SRA searches by title and by the authors' institutions turn up nothing matching 745 genomes, and no deposit was found in the Chinese National Genomics Data Center, Zenodo or Dryad. Even with an accession in hand the project would still fail A6 (raw whole-genome reads for 745 animals, tens of terabytes, and the rules forbid downloading raw sequencing) and A2 (body size and cold tolerance are population-level descriptions and literature-derived loci, not a measured per-animal column).
